text: Temporary Separation. Sometimes it may be wise to remove yourself, for a time, from the people or group that you normally would get answers from. Some people come back later on different terms, and sometimes the break has to be long-term because the pattern of losing yourself with them is deeply entrenched. As you differentiate, you learn to tell which of those apply. You want to be able to let the quiet little preferences that you have bubble up to the surface and know for sure that you’re not going by what your social group would want you to do.

Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end? If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can. text: We can not force forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. However, if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We remember that it can all be true at once. They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it, and our boundary with them still matters, but one day we may find that we have forgiven them, or at least that we’re not being run by the resentment anymore. And we don’t have to forgive first to get safe, set boundaries, hold someone accountable, get justice or get better.
